new.md:
Creates a new `GtkTextChildAnchor`.

Usually you would then insert it into a `GtkTextBuffer` with
[`TextBuffer.insert_child_anchor()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextBuffer#method:insert_child_anchor). To perform the
creation and insertion in one step, use the convenience
function [`TextBuffer.create_child_anchor()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextBuffer#method:create_child_anchor).

new_with_replacement.brief: Creates a new `GtkTextChildAnchor` with the given replacement character.
new_with_replacement.md:
Creates a new `GtkTextChildAnchor` with the given replacement character.

Usually you would then insert it into a `GtkTextBuffer` with
[`TextBuffer.insert_child_anchor()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.TextBuffer#method:insert_child_anchor).

doc.brief: Marks a spot in a `GtkTextBuffer` where child widgets can be “anchored”.
doc.md:
Marks a spot in a `GtkTextBuffer` where child widgets can be “anchored”.

The anchor can have multiple widgets anchored, to allow for multiple views.

get_deleted.brief: Determines whether a child anchor has been deleted from the buffer.
get_deleted.md:
Determines whether a child anchor has been deleted from
the buffer.

Keep in mind that the child anchor will be unreferenced
when removed from the buffer, so you need to hold your own
reference (with g_object_ref()) if you plan to use this
function — otherwise all deleted child anchors will also
be finalized.

get_widgets.brief: Gets a list of all widgets anchored at this child anchor.
get_widgets.md:
Gets a list of all widgets anchored at this child anchor.

The order in which the widgets are returned is not defined.
